sourceNote: Rider-Waite-Smith ordering (Strength VIII, Justice XI). Keywords follow common modern RWS usage and A. E. Waite's 'Pictorial Key to the Tarot' (1910). The game uses tarot only as reflection prompts, never as prediction. Card art must be original, because later recolourings of the RWS deck are copyrighted.

cards.name: The Fool
cards.reflectionPrompt: If you could begin one thing fresh, without having to know how it ends, what would it be?

cards.name: The Magician
cards.reflectionPrompt: Which tools and skills do you already have, even ones you forget about?

cards.name: The High Priestess
cards.reflectionPrompt: What does a quiet voice inside you know that hasn't been said aloud?

cards.name: The Empress
cards.reflectionPrompt: How could you nurture yourself today the way you'd care for a garden?

cards.name: The Emperor
cards.reflectionPrompt: What structure or routine helps all of you feel steadier?

cards.name: The Hierophant
cards.reflectionPrompt: Which teachings have helped you? Which do you want to set down?

cards.name: The Lovers
cards.reflectionPrompt: What choice would honour the values your whole system shares?

cards.name: The Chariot
cards.reflectionPrompt: The chariot's two horses pull different ways, yet it moves. Where could parts of you agree on a direction?

cards.name: Strength
cards.reflectionPrompt: Strength here means gentleness. Where could softness be the brave thing?

cards.name: The Hermit
cards.reflectionPrompt: Is there a difference, for you, between restful solitude and lonely isolation?

cards.name: Wheel of Fortune
cards.reflectionPrompt: Seasons turn. What is changing now, and what has always come back around?

cards.name: Justice
cards.reflectionPrompt: If you were as fair to yourself as you are to a friend, what would you say?

cards.name: The Hanged Man
cards.reflectionPrompt: What looks different when you see it from another angle, or through another part's eyes?

cards.name: Death
cards.reflectionPrompt: Which chapter is ready to close, so that something new has room?
cards.gentleNote: In tarot, Death almost never means literal death. It's about one season ending so another can begin. If this card brings up heavy feelings, the Anchor menu is always here.

cards.name: Temperance
cards.reflectionPrompt: Temperance blends two cups into one. What could blend, gently, within you?

cards.name: The Devil
cards.reflectionPrompt: The chains on this card are loose. Is there a pattern that holds you less tightly than it seems?
cards.gentleNote: This card is about patterns and attachments. It isn't about evil, and it says nothing about who you are.

cards.name: The Tower
cards.reflectionPrompt: When something has fallen apart before, what helped you rebuild?
cards.gentleNote: The Tower can feel frightening. It's about structures that weren't serving you giving way, and it isn't a prediction of harm. If this card unsettles you, take a breath; the Anchor menu is always here.

cards.name: The Star
cards.reflectionPrompt: What small hope can you hold onto tonight?

cards.name: The Moon
cards.reflectionPrompt: When things feel unreal or uncertain, what helps you find the path?

cards.name: The Sun
cards.reflectionPrompt: What would let the youngest part of you feel safe enough to play?

cards.name: Judgement
cards.reflectionPrompt: Without harshness, what are you being called toward?

cards.name: The World
cards.reflectionPrompt: Wholeness can look many ways. What does feeling whole, as you are, mean to you?
